candidates.title: Machine creation accepts a configuration that starts at an rx-rejected manual yield, whose revert root hash is the hash of no state: the canonical hash becomes 0x00..00 and nothing after it can be claimed or proved
candidates.component: Machine creation from a configuration (machine::machine / validate_processor_shadow), with the rejection exception in collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, uarch_reset_state and the regenerated UArchReset.sol
candidates.role: Honest operator (machine creation, collectors, log producers). The verifiers (C++ replay, regenerated UArchReset) show the same successor, so no verifier-only rating applies.
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp: constructor register loading (~l.150-200: write_reg(iflags_Y), write_reg(htif_tohost), no revert root hash field in machine_config) and validate_processor_shadow (l.205-234: checks marchid/mvendorid/mimpid, x0, iunrep and padding only); src/rejected-manual-yield.hpp is_rejected_manual_yield; src/machine.cpp collect_mcycle_root_hashes l.2534-2538, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes l.2810-2835 (tail checked only by its last entry) and l.2944-2945; src/uarch-reset-state.cpp; solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src/EmulatorCompat.sol revertState/readRevertRootHash
candidates.description: The rejection exception replaces the content hash by the revert root hash whenever iflags_Y != 0 and tohost is a manual yield with reason rx-rejected. Every reachable rejected state got that hash from a state-changing delivery, so it is the hash of the state the input was delivered to. Machine creation does not enforce this: it accepts a reproducible Keccak configuration with processor.registers.iflags.Y = 1 and htif.tohost = (YIELD, MANUAL, RX_REJECTED), values the manual allows for those registers, while the revert root hash is not a configuration field and starts as 32 zero bytes (by reading the code it can also be any 32 bytes through a processor backing store; I did not test that path). On that machine the canonical hash at the next mcycle boundary is 0x00..00, the hash of no state. collect_mcycle_root_hashes returns it as the fixed-point leaf, log_reset_uarch / verify_reset_uarch / UArchReset return it as the after-hash, and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes can only be satisfied with a fabricated tail (it checks only that the last entry equals the revert root hash). For every later position the canonical state does not exist, so no node, uarch trajectory or step proof can be produced. R4 requires such a configuration to be rejected when the machine is created. This is a variant, at the rollup registers, of R1-R4-1 (creation accepting a non-pristine uarch).
candidates.trigger: Whoever creates a machine from a configuration (trusted caller) with iflags.Y = 1 and an rx-rejected manual-yield tohost, e.g. a template author storing a machine captured at a rejected yield of another run, or a hand-written configuration. No guest or input can produce it.
candidates.reachability: Unreachable from any valid template, with this argument: a valid template waits at a manual yield with the accepted reason; iflags_Y is set only by an HTIF manual-yield write and the interpreter stops at it on every path, so the only transition out of the template's fixed point is an advance-state delivery that changes the state; that delivery writes the revert root hash with the referee-supplied before-hash (A4), which is the content hash of the state it was delivered to; the guest cannot write the revert root hash (R8), and no later delivery changes the state until the next accepted yield. So every rejected yield reachable from a valid template carries the hash of a real state. The state exists only through the configuration accepted at creation, and such a machine is not itself a valid template (it does not wait at an accepted yield).

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. It is not a snapshot the emulator did not write, nor a deliberate API change: it is a configuration accepted at creation, which R4 covers explicitly: "Every reproducible configuration that the emulator accepts, using the deployment's hash function and holding only register values that the RISC-V specification and the manual allow, yields a machine on which this rule holds. A configuration that would not is rejected when the machine is created."
rating_steps.2_role: Honest operator: AUDIT.md lists "Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program, hash tree, log producers, collect_mcycle_root_hashes and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, input delivery, and storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines" in that role.
rating_steps.3_high_medium: Matches the High cases for demonstrably unreachable states ("A divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states" / "A crash, hang, or memory-safety defect in the emulator that only demonstrably unreachable states trigger" in spirit: the honest operator cannot compute the uarch claim or any proof from there). The unreachability argument is given under reachability. This is the preferred rating, as for R1-R4-1.
rating_steps.4_critical: Critical only under the reading R1-R4-1 also carries as its alternative: that accepting the configuration is itself an R4 violation on the honest operator's path ("A configuration that would not is rejected when the machine is created"), whatever the reachability of the state.
rating_steps.5_low: Low if triage reads R4's second bullet as covering only configurations that are valid templates (this one is not: it does not wait at an accepted yield).

candidates.claimed_severity: High (preferred: only at a demonstrably unreachable state) / Critical (creation-time acceptance read as an R4 violation by itself) / Low (if R4's configuration bullet covers valid templates only)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not break the goal from a valid template. It removes the margin R4 asks for: the emulator accepts a machine whose canonical hash is the hash of no state, after which the honest operator can produce neither a uarch-level claim nor a proof, and a dispute steered past that boundary can only end by timeout. R4 asks for rejection at creation precisely so that no accepted machine leaves the domain where claims and proofs exist.
candidates.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBCMIO/exp2.lua (run with bugs/env.sh): cartesi.machine{ram={length=1<<20}, processor={registers={iflags={Y=1}, htif={tohost=(HTIF_DEV_YIELD<<56)|(HTIF_YIELD_CMD_MANUAL<<48)|(HTIF_YIELD_MANUAL_REASON_RX_REJECTED<<32)}}}} is accepted; root hash 4f44a2c7..., read_revert_root_hash() = 00..00; collect_mcycle_root_hashes returns one hash 0000000000000000... with break reason yielded manually; collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes with an empty tail throws 'revert uarch tail is required' and accepts the made-up tail {'xyyy...', 32 zero bytes}; after run_uarch to halt, log_reset_uarch verifies (verify_reset_uarch) to after-hash 00..00.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: pcall(cartesi.machine, cfg) with the configuration above (reproducible, keccak256). Required: creation fails (or, if it succeeds, the machine's canonical hash at the fixed point, collect_mcycle_root_hashes(...).hashes[1], is the hash of a state the operator can hold, i.e. not a value that no machine hashes to). Today creation succeeds and the collected hash is 32 zero bytes: exit 1. A second assertion can repeat it with a processor backing store whose revert root hash holds 32 arbitrary bytes.

candidates.title: A non-advance delivery (inspect-state, or any other reason) never renews imcyclemax: an inspect runs on whatever mcycles the last advance left, none at all after an input that accepted on its last cycle, and the manual's host loop then never ends
candidates.component: Input delivery (send_cmio_response) and the manual's rollup host protocol (doc/README.md '#### Rollup', 'Rolling Cartesi Machines')
candidates.role: Honest operator for send_cmio_response as transition code, but the affected use (inspect-state) is off the verified history; the manual is the specification. Rated as a manual/behavior gap.
candidates.location: src/send-cmio-response.cpp l.60-68 (imcyclemax and the revert root hash are written only inside `if (reason == HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE)`); src/interpret.cpp interpret() l.6414 (mcycle >= imcyclemax returns before anything runs); doc/README.md host loop for inspect-state (~l.7836-7848: 'While register iflags_H is 0 and register iflags_Y is 0 ... Resume machine') and the imcyclemax register description (l.7384)
candidates.description: send_cmio_response with reason HTIF_YIELD_REASON_INSPECT_STATE (or any reason other than advance-state) writes the rx buffer and fromhost and clears iflags_Y, but leaves imcyclemax as the last advance-state delivery set it. This matches R6 (imcyclemax is written only by an advance-state delivery that changes the state), but it means an inspect query does not get a budget of its own: it can execute imcyclemax - mcycle instructions, i.e. what the previous input did not use, and zero when the previous input accepted exactly at imcyclemax (a state R5 treats as a normal accepted yield). The machine then stops at the mcycle-overflow fixed point with iflags_Y = 0 and iflags_H = 0, without a report or a manual yield. The manual does not say that inspects share the previous input's budget; its register text describes imcyclemax only as 'the inclusive mcycle limit', its delivery text does not mention the register (already recorded as R7-MANARCH-1 for advance), and its inspect host loop (resume while neither halted nor yielded manually) spins forever in this state, as the advance loop does (R7-MANLUA1-1). A template that never received an advance has imcyclemax = 2^64-1, so the same query behaves differently before and after the first input.
candidates.trigger: A node or tool that serves inspect-state queries on a snapshot of an application whose last accepted input used most or all of its 2^48-1 mcycles (the input sender can aim for that only in an application that lets input size drive its cycle usage up to the limit).
candidates.reachability: Reachable: an accepted yield at any mcycle up to and including imcyclemax is reachable (the guest chooses how many instructions it runs before accepting), and inspect deliveries are a documented use of the machine API. It never touches the verified history: advance-state deliveries renew the budget from the same state.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded by name. But R4 says: "Inspect-state requests are outside the verified history. Nothing from one may reach a state on the honest operator's path, and their results carry no guarantee." So the effect (an inspect that cannot finish) has no bearing on any claim.
rating_steps.2_role: send_cmio_response is input delivery (honest operator), but only its inspect use is affected; the manual's host loop is documentation.
rating_steps.3_high_medium: No listed High or Medium case fits. It is not "An undocumented deterministic deviation ... in behavior that no correct guest relies on" in a way that affects a correct guest in the verified history, and the manual's omission of imcyclemax from delivery is already R7-MANARCH-1.
rating_steps.4_critical: No rule or obligation is violated at a reachable state on the honest operator's path: R6 requires exactly this ("imcyclemax is likewise written only by such a delivery"), and R4 gives inspect results no guarantee.
rating_steps.5_low: Low: a real gap between the documented inspect protocol and the behavior (an inspect can be starved of cycles by the previous input, and the documented loop does not terminate), with no effect on the goal.

candidates.threat_to_goal: None on the goal of section 1. It is reported because the angle asked for the invariants of inspect: the invariant 'inspect leaves no trace' holds only through the operator's snapshot, and the emulator gives an inspect no cycle budget of its own, which the manual does not state.
candidates.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBCMIO/exp4.lua: on the bare-metal template (imcyclemax = 0xffffffffffffffff) an inspect delivery runs to an accepted yield. After one advance-state input, with imcyclemax lowered to mcycle + 20 to stand for an input that accepted late in its budget, send_cmio_response(INSPECT_STATE, 'query') leaves imcyclemax unchanged and run() returns BREAK_REASON_MCYCLE_OVERFLOW with iflags_Y = 0 and mcycle == imcyclemax. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBCMIO/exp3.lua shows the regenerated SendCmioResponse.sol and the C++ verifier agree with the emulator on these non-advance deliveries (4 accesses, no imcyclemax write).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua (documentation-level): build a guest that accepts an advance on the last cycle of its budget (or lower imcyclemax to mcycle through write_reg on a machine at an accepted yield), deliver an inspect and run the manual's inspect loop with a bound on iterations; assert that the loop ends (halt or manual yield) or that the manual states the shared budget. Today run() returns BREAK_REASON_MCYCLE_OVERFLOW at once and the documented loop never ends.

not_covered: Guest software (machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1): only libcmt rollup.c and io.c were re-read for the yield, rx and tx interface (pack/unpack of tohost and fromhost, finish/accept/reject, emit paths, rx length check). rollup-http-server, the rollup CLI, the yield tool and io-mock were not re-audited; the kernel /dev/cmio driver is out of scope.

collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes with log2_bundle_uarch_cycle_count > 0 across a rejection, and append_uarch_reset_root_hash's final-bundle case: read only; my differential ran bundle height 0 for the uarch collector (reject case, 34 mcycles, plus the extra tail period) and heights 0, 1, 3 for the mcycle collector (reject, exception, halt).

The uarch-level differential for the exception and halt stops did not finish in the time I gave it (only their mcycle-level parts ran); accept with outputs was not run through my differential at all (too many mcycles for per-mcycle hashing).
Rejection, accept or automatic yield exactly at an unsaturated imcyclemax (needs 2^48 mcycles); I only reasoned about it and ran delivery at saturating mcycle values on the EVM and C++ verifiers.

Dave's CartesiStateTransition was read, not executed on the chain harness; the delivery branches were run on the StepVerifier wrapper of the regenerated step only (all 20 cases match the emulator, including zero-length, 2 MiB, oversized, not yielded, rejected, exception, halted, saturating mcycle and non-advance reasons).
JSON-RPC send/log/verify_send_cmio_response and receive_cmio_request were read (oversized substitution, optional revert root hash, buffer bounds) but not run against a remote server.
The PRT player (prt.lua) and the cartesi-machine CLI rollup loops were read only where they deliver inputs, revert and sample rejected states; their claim builders were not exercised.

Native versus uarch agreement for HTIF writes with unusual tohost values (unknown device, cmd >= 64, halt with DATA bit 0 clear, disabled iyield bits) and for timer interrupts pending at a yield or fixed point: reasoned from the shared C++ code only, no differential run.
Soft yield and console-output breaks at fixed points were read (no state difference found), not tested.
log_step / verify_step (main-processor step log) at fixed points and rejections: read only, ZK path.

Observation not reported as a candidate: when an automatic yield lands exactly on imcyclemax, run() reports BREAK_REASON_MCYCLE_OVERFLOW and iflags_X stays 1 for good; the pending output or report is never surfaced as an automatic yield. A5 gives that tx-buffer content no meaning (stop at imcyclemax without a manual yield), so I found no rule it violates.
